children: India's National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) plans to raise funds through a debut 10-year U.S. dollar denominated bond issuance and has provided an initial price guidance, two merchant bankers said on Wednesday.
NaBFID has given an outlook for a spread of 130 basis points over 10-year U.S. Treasury yield.
The Indian financial institution would look to raise around $1 billion, through the bond sale, which would be under the central bank's discounted swap window.
In June, the Reserve Bank of India allowed banks and state-run companies to raise funds overseas and access a subsidised hedging facility, lowering the cost of managing currency risk.
Last week, state-run infrastructure financier's Managing Director Rajkiran Rai told Reuters that the bond issuance would be completed before end of September.
NaBFID is targeting a total fundraise of $4 billion before end of 2026
Of this, the infra lender has already raised $850 million through external commercial borrowing in August
The institution had raised $125 million via a smaller dollar loan tranche in March, which was its debut borrowing in the offshore market.
The bonds will be rated BBB by S&P, BBB– by Fitch Ratings and BBB+ by CareEdge, in line with the issuer's ratings.
